Description

This role will be on the Performance Consulting team in Knowledge and Development Solutions (KDS). Performance Consultant serves as a strategic partner to business leaders, helping identify, assess, and solve performance challenges that impact business results. This role works across a portfolio of business partners to diagnose needs, align solutions to organizational priorities, and drive initiatives from intake through implementation and measurement.

The Performance Consultant applies performance consulting principles to uncover root causes, recommend the right interventions, and ensure solutions create measurable business impact. Acting as a trusted advisor, the consultant collaborates with leaders, subject matter experts, and delivery partners to translate business strategy into capability-building initiatives that improve performance, accelerate organizational goals, and support long-term business outcomes.

**This role may have in-office requirements dependent upon candidate location.**
**This role level will be considered as a 16/17 range depending on candidate qualifications, skills and experience.**

Responsibilities:
- Build and maintain strong partnerships with business leaders and stakeholders to understand strategic priorities, identify performance opportunities, and serve as a trusted advisor on performance improvement strategies.
- Independently lead discovery, consultation, and analysis efforts to diagnose business challenges, identify root causes, and determine the most effective solutions to address performance needs
- Translate business objectives into actionable recommendations, leveraging the right mix of learning, coaching, communications, knowledge management, process improvement, and other performance enablement strategies when appropriate.
- Guide work through the intake, prioritization, and planning process, ensuring initiatives are aligned to business priorities, resource capacity, and expected outcomes.
- Provide oversight for assigned initiatives by coordinating stakeholders, establishing governance, managing risks and dependencies, and evaluating progress toward agreed-upon objectives.
- Partner with business leaders, subject matter experts, and delivery teams to prepare organizations for implementation and ensure solutions are launched effectively.
- Define success measures and evaluate outcomes to assess effectiveness, demonstrate business value, and inform future performance improvement efforts.
- Identify and communicate portfolio-level trends, risks, opportunities, and emerging business needs to help inform strategic decision-making and future investment priorities.
- Creates business documents for various presentations and meetings, especially for leadership.
- Works collaboratively with cross-functional stakeholders early and often, seeking constructive feedback and actively driving decision making.

Experience You Will Need:
- Experience partnering directly with senior business leaders and decision-makers to identify performance challenges, identify root causes, and recommend meaningful solutions.
- Experience problem solving and facilitating discovery conversations, gathering stakeholder requirements, and translating business needs into actionable recommendations.
- Demonstrated ability to use data and business performance metrics to inform recommendations and assess solution effectiveness.
- Strong business acumen with the ability to assess competing priorities, risks, dependencies, and organizational impacts.
- Proven ability to influence without authority and drive alignment among leaders, subject matter experts, and cross-functional partners.
- Experience presenting recommendations, project updates, and business cases to senior leadership audiences.
- Experience managing a portfolio of work while balancing strategic initiatives, operational priorities, and changing business demands.
- Strong relationship-building skills with a demonstrated ability to establish credibility and trust across multiple levels of the organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience in organizational effectiveness, change management, learning strategy, or business process improvement.

Description

Sr Claims Operations Manager - Casualty
Every claim tells a story about someone whose life just got harder - a car accident, a lawsuit, a loss they didn't see coming. Behind every one of those stories is an operation that has to run flawlessly under pressure. That's where the Sr Claims Operations Manager comes in.

As Sr Claims Operations Manager for Casualty , you'll be the connective tissue between Claims functional leadership and the operational muscle that makes their vision real. You'll turn strategy into results, coach a team of Claims Ops Managers to do the same and keep a sharp eye on the numbers that tell you whether the whole operation is actually working - for customers and for the people delivering on our promise to them.

*For I&S Roles, if you live within 50 miles of one of our hub locations, the expectation is twice a week in office.*
What you'll do
What you'll do
- Own the results. Review and monitor operational performance across your aligned Claims function, then build and roll out recommendations that improve customer service, retention, productivity and total cost management.
- Build the team you'd want to work for. Select top talent, coach continuously and hold your Claims Ops Managers accountable for developing their own people - because an engaging work environment starts with how you show up for your team.
- Partner across the business. Work closely with Claims functional leadership, operational staff, cross-functional leaders and outside stakeholders to bring projects and initiatives across the finish line.
- Champion the customer experience. Find the process efficiencies that make claims easier for customers and better for the business, while keeping every result compliant with the regulatory environment.
- Represent Claims Operations where it counts. Sit on department task forces and committees, act as the go-to liaison when issues come up, keep senior leaders in the loop and help shape planning and budget decisions.
- Lead the rollout. Manage training and implementation for Claims programs and initiatives - from new systems to efficiency plays.
- Step up when it matters most. Step up when it matters most. Take on special projects as they arise.

Why this role:
You'll have the backing of a company that's been protecting what matters to people since 1912 - and the room to shape how Claims Operations gets that job done. If you're ready to lead a team, sharpen an operation and make an impact people actually feel, we'd love to talk.

Qualifications

- Excellent organizational skills to coordinate activities and programs
- Demonstrated ability to communicate verbally and in writing at all levels of the organization and clearly and concisely express opinions, conclusions and recommendations
- In-depth knowledge of personal claims processes and procedures including branch office workflows, systems, roles and responsibilities required
- Excellent leadership, interpersonal, analytical, and negotiation skills required
- Bachelor`s degree plus 7-10 years of relevant and progressively more responsible work experience required
- Advanced insurance related designations/CPCU and/or advanced degree preferred

ES&I Operations is currently searching for a Senior Business Analyst or Project Manager I to support the day-to-day business operations of our Corporate Strategy & Research (CS&R) group including management of key vendor relationships, leading the planning & execution of department meetings, targeted metrics reporting including overall performance scorecard, crystalizing insights into executive-level PowerPoint presentations and dashboards, and team culture building initiatives. This is a great opportunity for an energetic individual to join a dynamic, tight-knit enterprise strategy and innovation community where you will lead key initiatives to enable a high-performance and vibrant team environment.

Responsibilities

- Lead the planning and execution of CS&R monthly department meetings to promote a culture of knowledge sharing, ensuring work alignment & transparency, and building a more unified and connected team

- Drive focus and discipline on expense management by supporting annual ES&I budget / planning process, serve as CS&R escalation path for expense inquiries, and coordinate timely CS&R payments (Ariba, Wire)
- Drive operational excellence, with a focus on productivity, effectiveness, and continuous improvement opportunities within CS&R by serving as point of contact / escalation path for all technology & tools matters including administration (e.g., SharePoint, Teams, Gen AI access); ensure full execution of consulting project teams onboarding & offboarding process including knowledge management

Description

The VP, Sr Dir, Finance Technology reports to the CIO, Corporate Technology and leads the technology strategy, portfolio, and organization supporting Global Finance. Global Finance Technology (GFT) enables the mission-critical processing and analysis of Liberty Mutual's ~$50B in annual revenue, and this leader will shape the modern platforms, data capabilities, and AI-enabled experiences that support Liberty's Finance transformation through 2030 and beyond. This is an opportunity to join Liberty Mutual at a pivotal moment in its Technology transformation, with the mandate, scale, and executive visibility to help modernize how we operate, makes decisions, and create enterprise value.

The role is accountable for both transformation and execution, modernizing and simplifying the Finance technology landscape across general ledger, accounting, treasury, tax, reinsurance, data, and enterprise risk and actuarial, while maintaining secure, stable, and resilient operations. The leader will oversee an organization of approximately 220 employees and 300 contractors, with an annual technology investment of approximately $200M, and partner closely with the Liberty’s Office of the CFO community to translate business priorities into measurable outcomes.

This is a senior technology leadership role requiring credibility across engineering, enterprise platforms, data, architecture, and AI, at a scale and breadth spanning multiple core financial ecosystems and global business units spanning ~29 countries. Equally important is the ability to influence and challenge executives, navigate complexity, make difficult tradeoffs, and lead teams through sustained, multi-year transformation. The successful candidate will build a high-performing, inclusive organization and create clarity, accountability, and momentum across a broad ecosystem of internal teams and external partners. The role requires a holistic leadership approach and breadth of perspective, drawing on enterprise and industry trends, to enable a high-performing, adaptable technology function and a data-first culture, led with an inclusive culture that fosters innovation, trust, people development, and integrity.

What This Role Is Accountable For:

1. Transformation Through Technology Execution
- Lead the modernization and simplification of the end-to-end Finance technology ecosystem: general ledger, accounting, treasury, tax, reinsurance, enterprise risk and actuarial, data, integration, security, and the Finance vendor landscape
- Drive transformation across central and business-unit-specific financial ecosystems in a mixed legacy and modern environment, balancing large 3rd-party software partnerships (SAP experience a plus) with custom, cloud-native solutions
- Make durable platform decisions that reduce structural risk, improve resilience, and compound value through 2030 and beyond, balancing near-term delivery with multi-year modernization
- Ensure Finance system, technical, and product architectures stay aligned with business objectives

2. Strategic Partnership & Constructive Challenge
- Act as a trusted technology and transformation partner to Liberty's CFO community and Finance leadership, co-owning outcomes, not just delivery, and shape how leaders think about technology, data, AI, and operating models
- Challenge functional leaders constructively and directly, bringing clarity to tradeoffs, sequencing, and change absorption across a multi-year Finance transformation
- Build partnerships with Finance leaders, vendors, and technology peers, and move leaders forward even amid ambiguity or resistance

3. Outcome-Driven Delivery & Accountability
- Own execution and results across the Finance technology investment portfolio (~$200M annual) and a technology organization of ~220 employees plus ~300 contractors
- Jointly set financial targets with Finance partners and ensure programs, including multiple multi-year initiatives, deliver to plan
- Ensure investments translate into measurable outcomes: speed, quality, control, productivity, and economics
- Drive disciplined prioritization, dependency management, resource allocation, and delivery rigor across teams and partners accountable for outcomes, not activity

4. Technology Excellence & Ecosystem Leadership
- Serve as an active member of the Corporate Technology function and Liberty Mutual Technology's Extended Leadership Team, contributing a Finance perspective to Liberty Mutual's enterprise technology agenda
- Champion Liberty Mutual Technology's strategic priorities and translate enterprise strategy into Finance execution: high-performing engineering, AI-enabled SDLC evolution, modern architecture, and resilient operations
- Lead adoption of modern engineering practices: product-centric delivery, platform thinking, automation, and AI across the SDLC
- Apply and evolve enterprise standards for architecture, security, data, and AI, balancing consistency with the realities of Finance transformation
- Craft and deliver an enterprise data strategy, anticipate technology evolution, and ensure Finance decisions strengthen the broader Liberty Mutual technology ecosystem

5. Talent, Culture & Change Leadership
- Build and lead a high-performing Finance technology organization that thrives in sustained transformation
- Build a flexible, adaptable workforce strategy (headcount, skills, experience, and full-time/professional-services mix) focused on skills for the future, and hire, develop, and coach the next line of technology leaders
- Foster a culture of direct communication, learning, inclusion, and execution excellence, and model courage in addressing conflict and making hard calls

Qualifications

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in a technical or business discipline, or equivalent experience; Master's preferred
- Minimum 15 years of related experience, including 5+ years in senior technology leadership
- Seasoned technology leader with a proven record leading large-scale, multi-year transformations in complex, regulated environments, with deep finance and insurance business acumen and understanding of how technology can be leveraged to support business strategy
- Demonstrated ability to influence, challenge, and partner with executives on operating models, sequencing, investment tradeoffs, and change absorption, addressing conflict directly for better outcomes
- Hands-on credibility across 3rd-party platform implementations (SAP experience a plus) and cloud-native, homegrown solutions (full-stack AWS, data transformation, data warehousing, and business intelligence/reporting)
- Proven experience crafting and delivering an enterprise data strategy
- Proven change leader who has built resilient, high-performing teams through sustained transformation, and translates vision into actionable deliverables
- Strong vendor and ecosystem leadership, selection, governance, and value realization across major Finance platforms and delivery partners (software, consulting, and outsourcing)
- Financial and operational acumen, including ownership of multi-year technology investment portfolios (labor, compute, software) and blended workforce strategies
- Ability to partner closely and establish strong, trusted working relationships to make impacts beyond technology. E.g., contributing to the larger Finance transformation at Liberty
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, able to go deep while staying focused on the big picture
- Effective, highly articulate communicator able to convey important messages verbally and in writing to all organizational levels

Only open to US-based employees.

Description

The Company
Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is the investment firm for Liberty Mutual Group (Liberty) and  is responsible for  powering Liberty’s strategy amid profound  change  in global capital markets. With deep expertise in fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies, LMI invests $120+ billion ( as of 12/31/2025 ) of capital globally, taking a long-term approach across its integrated platform and has a team of over 3 50  investment, finance, and operations professionals located in Boston, MA, and New York, NY.

LMI has a clear purpose: build enduring businesses side-by-side with our partners, drive economic growth, and generate superior risk-adjusted returns that power Liberty’s strategy and secure its promises. We offer the best of both worlds — the look and feel of a boutique investment firm with the reputation and financial strength of a global leader. As the investment firm of a mutual with long-term capital, LMI has a single client mandate. This gives us the freedom to focus on what we do best.

Our portfolio spans a broad spectrum of public and private investments, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and our toolkit in support of our mission. We invest across diverse asset classes, financial structures, and industries, including real estate, digital infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy, and technology—with the aim of creating value and powering innovation. We pride ourselves on our extensive network of mutually beneficial partnerships, and we use our substantial influence, capital, and energy to drive towards a better future. #LMI #LI-LMI

The Position:
The Business Transformation team serves as LMI's operating model and process design capability. Reporting to the Head of Business Transformation, this role serves as a strategic partner to senior leaders across the enterprise, helping design the operating models, governance structures and business capabilities that enable execution of LMI’s 2030 strategy. The role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, with depth in operating model and process design and a bias toward enabling near-term execution while shaping long-term direction. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable facilitating executive workshops, assessing complex investment lifecycles, designing governance frameworks, developing business capabilities and leading implementation efforts that deliver measurable business outcomes.
Responsibilities
- Lead enterprise design engagements. Lead complex, cross-functional engagements from discovery through implementation. Frame problems, align stakeholders, develop recommendations, and translate strategic objectives into operating models, roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
- Partner across Strategy & Execution. Operate within GIS Strategy & Execution, which brings together Business Transformation, Program Management, and Vendor Management. Lead both standalone organizational design engagements and serve as the embedded design partner on Program Management-governed programs, contributing operating model, capability, and governance design within a shared delivery model.
- Design target operating models. Develop target operating models that define operating processes, governance frameworks, decision rights, roles and responsibilities, and accountability models across investment and operational functions, including the organizational structures that support them.
- Drive process and business architecture. Assess and mature business capabilities and the processes that run them across the enterprise, identifying gaps, dependencies, and opportunities to improve scalability, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. Establish capability-based frameworks that support strategic planning and prioritization.
- Assess and optimize investment operations. Conduct end-to-end assessments of investment processes and operating workflows across public and private market asset classes. Identify root causes of operational challenges and develop practical, scalable solutions.
- Establish governance and performance frameworks. Define governance structures, success metrics, KPIs, reporting cadences, and operating routines that enable sustainable execution, accountability, and continuous improvement.
- Facilitate executive alignment. Lead workshops, working sessions, and stakeholder engagements that bring together diverse perspectives, build alignment, and accelerate decision-making across teams.
- Advance AI-enabled ways of working. Identify and scale opportunities to apply AI-enabled tools and methods across the function, improving how engagements are delivered and enabling faster, more scalable analysis and design.
- Bring external perspective and industry insight. Monitor industry trends, emerging operating models, technology innovations, and leading practices across asset management and financial services to inform strategic recommendations and future-state design.

Qualifications

- 10+ years in asset management, investment operations, process design, operating model design, business architecture, or management consulting, with at least 3 years owning complex engagements end-to-end through a structured methodology.
- Direct experience working in or advising asset management, institutional investing, insurance investment management, or investment operations organizations.
- Deep understanding of institutional asset management and investment operations, including front-, middle-, and back-office operating models.
- Experience supporting public and private market investment businesses, including credit, structured products, private markets, limited partnerships, alternatives, or related investment strategies.
- Demonstrated success leading complex initiatives with enterprise-wide impact.
- Experience designing and implementing operating models, governance structures, organizational frameworks, capability models, or large-scale business process redesigns.
- Demonstrated fluency with AI-enabled tools applied to delivery work, such as synthesizing interview readouts, drafting process maps and operating model artifacts, and generating RACIs and other structured deliverables.
- Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence senior leaders and facilitate alignment across competing priorities.
- Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, solve complex problems, and drive measurable results.

Preferred Experience
- Experience within a leading asset manager, insurance investment organization, institutional investment platform, or top-tier consulting firm serving investment management clients.
- Expertise in business architecture, capability modeling, organizational design, operating model design, or enterprise methodologies.
- Experience supporting strategic initiatives involving operating model modernization, business capability development, data transformation, product operating models, investment platform modernization, or organizational redesign.
- Familiarity with investment platforms and technologies such as SimCorp, Aladdin, Anaplan, eFront, EDM, Wall Street Office, Moody's, or related systems.
- Advanced degree in Business, Finance, Organizational Effectiveness, Strategy, or a related discipline.

- Most transformation roles stop at strategy or org charts. We design how an entire investment organization operates and then help put it into practice.
- You will work across investment teams, operations, finance, product, data and technology to solve some of LMI’s most complex strategic challenges, from defining target operating models for emerging asset classes to establishing governance frameworks for enterprise-wide initiatives.
- The team works from a codified methodology, including a target operating model playbook, a capability evolution playbook and a 26-deliverable framework for operating model engagements, so design work is rigorous and repeatable rather than reinvented for each engagement. Your work will directly influence how LMI scales, executes and competes in the years ahead. If you are energized by solving complex organizational problems, shaping enterprise strategy and building the operating models that enable investment organizations to perform at their best, we encourage you to apply.

Travel

10%

Our portfolio spans a broad spectrum of public and private investments, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and our toolkit in support of our mission. We invest across diverse asset classes, financial structures, and industries, including real estate, digital infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy, and technology—with the aim of creating value and powering innovation. We pride ourselves on our extensive network of mutually beneficial partnerships, and we use our substantial influence, capital, and energy to drive towards a better future.  #LMI #LI-LMI
The Position
Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is seeking an experienced operations and controls professional to join our Investment Operations function as Vice President, Operational Excellence. This is a newly created, high-impact role purpose-built to assess and strengthen the health of daily operations across the full investment operations platform.

This role serves as the function’s first-line lead for operational health — responsible for evaluating operational risk, testing the effectiveness of the controls designed to mitigate that risk, identifying process and control gaps, and driving their remediation to closure across all operating teams: Treasury Services, Cash & Trade Operations, Derivatives Operations, Loan Operations, Alternatives Operations, Shared Services, and Investment Accounting Operations. The role reports to the Head of Investment Accounting Operations, with its function-wide mandate sponsored by the Head of Operational Strategy & Delivery.

Beyond assessment, the role owns the operational KPI and metrics framework and the operational-health reporting that informs functional governance, and partners closely with Strategy & Execution’s Transformation team to convert findings into durable, delivered fixes.
This is a first-line operational-excellence role embedded in the business; it coordinates with — and is distinct from — second-line Risk and Internal Audit, and does not provide independent assurance. The ideal candidate is a skilled collaborator who understands the downstream impact of operational decisions and can influence peer teams without direct authority. This is a high-impact individual contributor role with the opportunity to grow into a people management capacity as the function scales.

Key Responsibilities
- Operational Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) - Design and run a recurring, first-line risk and control self-assessment across all seven operating teams, producing a current-state view of where daily execution is fragile
- Maintain a living map of operational risks, the controls intended to mitigate them, and the residual risk that remains after those controls
- Bring an industry-aware lens to what strong operational controls look like across asset classes and lifecycle stages

- Control Effectiveness & Gap Remediation - Test whether controls are operating as designed
- Identify process and control gaps, prioritize them at the function level based on risk, and own them through to closure
- Trace the upstream root causes of downstream breaks and not-in-good-order conditions, championing systemic, durable fixes over one-off corrections
- Document assessment evidence

- Metrics, KPIs & Operational-Health Reporting - Own the operational KPI framework and the run-state operational-health reporting that feeds functional governance forums
- Translate operational data into a clear, decision-ready view of functional health for senior leadership
- Align metrics and definitions consistently across teams and systems of record

- Transformation & Product Partnership - Serve as the demand-side partner to Strategy & Execution’s Transformation team, converting diagnosed gaps into a prioritized remediation backlog
- Coordinate with Product Owners to ensure product backlogs reflect operations requirements and priorities
- Ensure delivered solutions close the underlying operational risk rather than addressing symptoms
- Identify and advance automation and process-improvement opportunities, including practical application of AI tooling

- Governance, Escalation & Second-Line Coordination - Run the operational-health governance routine (chaired and sponsored by the Head of OS&D), presenting current-state assessment, open gaps, and remediation status with items assigned to process owners and dates
- Proactively raise operational risks, process concerns, and stakeholder impacts in a constructive, solutions-oriented manner
- Coordinate with second-line Risk and Internal Audit to align scope and avoid duplication of assurance activity

- Cross-Functional Collaboration & Partner Performance - Serve as a trusted operational partner and subject-matter expert across investment, accounting, technology, data, and treasury teams
- Assess the operational performance of external service providers through a risk-and-control lens
- Communicate process changes, improvement initiatives, and strategic priorities clearly to senior stakeholders

Qualifications

- Education - Bachelor’s degree in finance, Business, Accounting, or a related field
- Advanced degree (e.g., MBA) a plus
- Relevant risk/controls or process-improvement certifications (e.g., Lean Six Sigma) preferred but not required

- 10+ years of experience in investment operations, financial operations, or operational risk and controls, ideally within an asset manager, insurer, alternative investment firm, or comparable institutional investment platform
- Demonstrated experience in operational risk assessment, control design and effectiveness testing, or RCSA-type programs
- Strong understanding of the investment operations lifecycle across multiple asset classes — including loans, derivatives, alternatives, and cash/treasury
- Experience defining and operating metrics and KPIs and translating operational data into governance-ready reporting
- Familiarity with loan administration and accounting systems, IBOR and ABOR environments, and how data flows across a multi-system operations infrastructure
- Highly effective collaborator with proven experience influencing peer teams without direct authority in a matrixed organization; able to raise risks and represent stakeholder perspectives in a constructive, solutions-oriented manner

Risk Financing sits at the center of how Liberty Mutual transfers risk to the reinsurance market, and its effectiveness depends on a large number of functions moving in step. This role exists to make that happen. As Reinsurance Operations Manager, you will be the connective tissue between Risk Financing and its key partner functions — Enterprise Risk Management, RI Operations, RI Accounting, Legal, Tax, LM Re and the broker community — ensuring that priorities are clearly set, actively managed and consistently executed across all of them.
This is a role for someone who is energized by turning recurring friction into durable process. You will own the definition of the treaty lifecycle and its implementation across the team, contribute to the standard operating procedures that allow placement teams to act with confidence, and take a leading role in renewal preparation and management — including the treaty handover to downstream teams within agreed service levels. You will work across the full lifecycle, from market approval and reinsurer governance through binding, post-placement data delivery and in-force management.
Much of the work involves shaping the agenda of teams you do not manage, so the ability to build credibility, communicate with clarity in writing and in person, and hold a position under senior scrutiny is central to success.
What you'll do
- Serve as a key operational point of contact between Risk Financing and its partner functions, establishing and maintaining a governed cadence with each
- Own the treaty lifecycle definition end to end and drive its adoption across the Risk Financing team
- Author, secure approval for and implement standard operating procedures and standardized templates that remove ambiguity and reduce duplication of work
- Own operational renewal preparation and management for reinsurance cycles, including new process implementation, training, and monitoring of operational handovers to Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and RI Operations withing tight SLAs
- Partner with ERM on reinsurer governance, collateral requirements, approved market lists and concentration frameworks, and implement approved changes as business as usual
- Support regulatory and control processes including SSAP62 risk transfer reviews, transfer pricing documentation and internal audit requests
- Drive data quality and standardization initiatives with internal teams and external delivery partners
- Identify and champion opportunities to simplify how the team delivers, including responsible adoption of GenAI tooling

At least 75% of time is spent on a combination of the following responsibilities:
- Operational excellence and SOP ownership: Own, maintain and continuously improve Risk Financing standard operating procedures across the treaty lifecycle, ensuring processes are clearly documented, scalable, audit ready and consistently applied globally.
- Process optimisation and waste reduction: Identify inefficiencies, duplication and bottlenecks across Risk Financing operations, applying continuous improvement methods to simplify processes, reduce manual effort, minimise rework and shorten cycle times.
- Automation and simplification: Lead workflow simplification initiatives in partnership with Technology, Data and operational teams, translating strategic priorities into practical improvements.
- Data, reporting and insight: Improve data quality, lineage and usability across reinsurance systems and reporting outputs, using descriptive analytics, visualisation tools, KPIs and operational metrics to support decision making and executive reporting.
- Stakeholder and partner connectivity: Act as a central coordinator between Risk Financing and partner functions including Finance, Claims, Actuarial, Legal, Tax, brokers and reinsurers, ensuring smooth handoffs, clear ownership and aligned timelines.
- Governance, controls and risk management: Support operational risk identification and remediation, ensuring controls, documentation and governance are in place to meet internal, audit and regulatory expectations.
- Operational performance management: Develop, update and analyse complex metrics used to assess operational performance, productivity, staffing needs, service levels and other measures valuable to Risk Financing leadership.
- Audit, review and senior forum support: Prepare materials, insights and recommendations for audits, reviews, governance meetings and senior forums
- Innovation and continuous improvement: Champion new tools, ways of working and data-driven practices across Risk Financing Operations, embedding continuous improvement into daily management.
- Mentoring and capability building: Provide guidance, coaching and mentoring to less experienced staff, helping embed consistent operational practices across the Risk Financing team.

Qualifications

- Competencies typically acquired through a Bachelor`s degree or equivalent experience in addition to 8+ years of relevant experience to include reinsurance operations, process improvement, accounting or audit
- Substantial experience in reinsurance operations, treaty administration or a closely related insurance operations discipline
- Advanced degree preferred
- Displays strong research, problem solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills
- Advanced business operations knowledge to include understanding the function`s value chain and market conditions
- Advanced influencing, relationship management & presentation skills
- Highly skilled at supporting change and imparting value within an organization
- Strong project management skills as part of implementing business process changes
- Advanced knowledge of available data sources, strengths and shortcomings
- May also be relevant based on the particular needs of the position: Advanced knowledge of Excel and strong knowledge of database software
- Solid knowledge of business intelligence tools
- A demonstrated record of cross-functional coordination in a complex organization, including influencing teams outside your reporting line

- Excellent written and verbal communication, with the judgement to adapt the same material for operational, financial and risk-and-controls audiences

- Comfort operating with autonomy and precision on long-horizon initiatives alongside a high volume of ad hoc requests

Description

Global Risk Solutions writes business in more than 20 countries, and the controls behind that business have to hold up everywhere. This role owns a meaningful piece of how we prove they do and how we keep proving it faster, using the AI tools now built into the way our team works.

This is a role for someone who genuinely likes both halves of controls work: the analytical half, where you dig into a process and find the gap nobody else noticed, and the influencing half, where you bring a business owner along without owning their process or their decision. You'll partner with underwriting, claims, compliance and finance leaders across North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia Pacific  and with external program partners, where you'll often be the Liberty Mutual voice in the room.

The opportunity
You'll help lead how GRS assures and strengthens its control environment worldwide driving the resolution of audit findings, elevating the quality of account reconciliations, building attestation programs from the ground up, and leading controls audits of our program partners. Alongside all of it, you'll bring a builder's mindset to how the work itself gets done: using GenAI to take on the mechanical lift so more of your time and your team's goes toward judgment, not formatting.

Where you'll make an impact

- Audit remediation & assurance   -   Serve as GRS's connective tissue with Global Internal Audit — keeping findings, action plans and closure evidence moving toward resolution, and escalating where the risk warrants it.

- - Support the external audit process- Coordinating request, resolving open items with external auditor on a timely basis.

- Controls & attestation quality    - Raise the bar on the controls framework across GRS strengthening account reconciliations and attestation coverage across entities and extending that same rigor to every project and initiative the business takes on.
- Turn documentation, process gaps and structural weaknesses into durable fixes.

- Program partner oversight    - Plan and lead controls audits of external program partners, testing what they report against what actually happens and following up until remediation is real.

- AI-augmented analysis - Put GenAI to work on reshaping data, drafting first-pass analysis and getting up to speed on technical findings quickly then build repeatable AI workflows the rest of the team can use too.

- People leadership
- - Coach and develop team members, including across significant time-zone gaps, building their judgment so they can make sound calls independently.

Built around AI, not bolted on

Liberty Mutual is investing heavily in AI across the enterprise, and GRS Financial Controls is one of the places that shift shows up first. This role sits right at that intersection: you'll use GenAI to compress the time spent on mechanical work reshaping files, comparing narratives across entities, drafting the first version of an observation and apply the time you get back to the calls that actually need a human. You'll also help set the pattern for the rest of the team, turning one-off prompts into repeatable processes others can pick up and trust.

This position reports to Livian Selau
